title: Transferring a design with a heat-erasable pen
subtitle: Drawing a design onto fabric with a pen whose marks vanish when heat is applied.
excerpt: A heat-erasable pen makes marks that disappear when touched with a warm iron or a hair dryer. You trace or draw the design before stitching, then remove the marks with heat when the work is finished. The marks can return in cold conditions, so a final steam iron is essential.
sourceNotes: Technique based on contemporary needlework practice. Heat-erasable pens are a 20th-century development.

glossaryTerms.definition: Fabric pen marks that disappear when heat is applied. The ink is thermo-chromic: it becomes colourless above a certain temperature. In very cold conditions the colour can reappear, so a steam iron is needed to set the removal permanently.

content.text: on fabric that disappear when touched with a warm iron. The pen draws as freely as a ballpoint, giving you good control for fine designs and small lettering.

items.name: Iron or hair dryer (to remove marks)
Light box or window for tracing (optional)

content.text: Test the pen on a scrap of the same fabric. Apply heat to check the marks disappear cleanly, then chill the swatch in the freezer for one minute to confirm the marks do not reappear.
Trace or draw the design directly onto the fabric with the heat-erasable pen.
Mount the fabric in a hoop and stitch the design.
When stitching is complete, press the piece with a warm iron on the reverse side. The marks will vanish within a few seconds.
Steam press a second time to ensure the marks are permanently gone and won't reappear if the piece is stored in a cold room.

items.cause: The piece was stored in a cold room or freezer before a final steam press.
items.fix: Steam press again. The pigment reverts in cold conditions. Always steam press after cold storage.

items.symptom: The marks don't disappear fully on delicate fabric
items.cause: The fabric cannot tolerate the heat needed to erase the ink.
items.fix: Use a water-soluble pen instead on silk and delicate fabrics. Test the erasure on a scrap before stitching the full design.

content.text: Heat-erasable pens suit lettering and small text where fine pen control matters. You can add lines mid-project, remove them, and re-draw without wetting the fabric.
